notes: Both agree the genome-wide screen methodology and hit identification (C3, C45-C49, C86) are rigorous and well-validated. LLM includes additional claims about pulse-chase experiments and statistical methods, but core screening claims show full agreement.

Strong agreement on TRPM5-NCX coupling mechanism (C10-C13, C69-C71, C114, C120-C121). Both find the mechanistic evidence convincing, though peer reviewers qualify this as applicable 'at least in colonic cell line context.' Shared claims represent the core mechanistic findings.

Disagreement on extracellular calcium requirement (C8, C9, C59, C60, C62). LLM finds evidence well-demonstrated, but peer reviewers question generalizability, citing airway epithelium literature showing calcium entry is not acutely important. Peer reviewers uncertain whether findings apply beyond colonic cells.

Disagreement on TRPM5's role in MUC5AC secretion (C4, C5, C52, C58). LLM finds multiple lines of evidence supporting TRPM5's role, but peer reviewers express concern that 2hr PMA stimulation could introduce artifacts and may measure induced rather than constitutive secretion. Reviewers request cycloheximide experiments.

Partial overlap on TRPM5 mechanism claims (C6, C7, C55, C56). Both support the mechanistic findings where they overlap, but LLM R3 focuses on TRPM5 knockdown effects while peer R2 emphasizes the broader TRPM5-NCX coupling. Agreement on shared claims but different grouping contexts.

Disagreement on MUC5AC secretion assay validation (C42, C43, C44). LLM finds assay well-validated with appropriate controls, but peer reviewers question whether PMA stimulation protocol measures constitutive secretion or introduces artifacts through new protein synthesis. Only 3 claims overlap; represents different aspects of assay concerns.

Minimal overlap (C63, C64, C65) on calcium-related mechanisms. Both support the mechanistic findings in their respective contexts, but represent different thematic groupings - LLM R4 focuses on calcium entry requirement while peer R2 addresses broader TRPM5-NCX mechanism.

LLM identifies speculative claims about SILV, TAB1/MAPK15, and GPCR/ion channel functions (C99, C100, C101) as UNCERTAIN, requiring additional validation. No corresponding peer review result addresses these specific claims.

Both address assay validation but with different claim sets. LLM R1 covers comprehensive assay validation (C32-C44, C83) while peer R1 focuses on screening methodology (C3, C45-C49, C86). Only C42-C44 overlap, but peer reviewers later question PMA protocol (see peer R5).

Peer reviewers raise concerns about physiological relevance and generalizability (C1, C14, C16-C18, C30, C31, C74) - MUC5AC not normally produced by colonic epithelium. These broader contextual concerns about cell model appropriateness are not explicitly addressed as a grouped evaluation in LLM results.
